definition: The use of clever but misleading arguments to deceive

definition: Superficially plausible but actually wrong or misleading

definition: The use of ambiguous language to conceal the truth

definition: The use of many words where fewer would do; evasive speech

definition: A roundabout way of expressing something that could be said simply

definition: Using too many words; tediously long-winded

definition: Using very few words; brief and concise

definition: Translucently clear; easy to understand; lucid

definition: Difficult to understand; obscure in meaning

definition: A grammatical mistake or breach of good manners

definition: The action of changing one's loyalties; making conflicting statements

definition: Speaking or acting in an evasive way; deliberate avoidance of truth

definition: The action of making something unclear or unintelligible

definition: To deny or contradict; to speak against or oppose

definition: A formal written defense of one's opinions or conduct

definition: A form of reasoning where a conclusion follows from two premises

definition: A concise statement expressing a general truth or observation

definition: A remark so overused that it carries no meaning; a cliché

definition: A lengthy, aggressive, and critical speech

definition: A bitter, impassioned verbal attack against a person

definition: A long, mournful lament or complaint

definition: Of doubtful authenticity; probably fictional though widely circulated

definition: Not candid or sincere; pretending ignorance or innocence

definition: Using more words than necessary to convey meaning

definition: A logical fallacy made by the speaker without awareness

definition: The concentration of mental energy and desire on a particular object or idea

example: The fulcrum of the negotiation was the timeline — everything else adjusted around it.

definition: The protection, backing, or support of a person or organization
example: The project moved forward under the aegis of the CEO, which meant it moved forward.

definition: Most noticeable or important; prominent
example: The most salient fact — that they'd done this before and failed — was not included in the deck.

definition: Relating to a transitional or initial stage; occupying a threshold position
example: The organization existed in a liminal state — no longer what it was, not yet what it claimed to be.

definition: A person who takes part in a dialogue or conversation
example: The most useful interlocutor in the negotiation said the least and understood the most.

definition: Descended from the same ancestor; of the same lineage
example: The rival companies were consanguineous — both founded by alumni of the same failed startup.

definition: To dispute the truth, validity, or honesty of something
example: She didn't disagree with the conclusion — she impugned the methodology that produced it.

definition: Harsh criticism or censure; public disgrace
example: The regulatory finding brought opprobrium that the PR team spent a year attempting to reframe.

definition: To criticize severely; to censure harshly
example: The review excoriated the product in language so precise it read like a legal brief.

definition: To make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve
example: The update ameliorated the performance issue without addressing any of the design ones.

definition: To make a problem or bad situation worse
example: The fix exacerbated the original issue and introduced three new ones — a net loss.

definition: The presence of something in only small or insufficient quantities
example: The paucity of evidence did not slow the confidence of the conclusion.

definition: An excessive amount of something; a supply exceeding what is appropriate
example: A surfeit of meetings is how organizations perform the idea of work without doing it.

definition: Speaking or representing the truth; truthful
example: The veracious account of what happened was shorter than every official version combined.

definition: The tendency to be untruthful; habitual lying
example: The investor deck demonstrated a mendacity so confident it almost constituted a vision.

definition: Constant or close attention to what one is doing; diligent application
example: Her assiduity was the kind that makes everyone around them reconsider their own output.

definition: Excessive confidence or boldness; audacity
example: He had the temerity to invoice for the advice they hadn't asked for and hadn't followed.

definition: Insolent or impertinent behavior; brazen boldness
example: The effrontery of the follow-up email, three hours after the rejection, deserved its own case study.

definition: The quality of being impudent; disrespectful boldness
example: His impudence in the meeting was either confidence or a misread of the room — the outcome would clarify.

definition: Lack of respect; rudeness; irrelevance to the matter at hand
example: The impertinence of the question was its virtue — everyone else had been too polite to ask it.

definition: Showing a willingness to take bold risks; daring
example: The audacious pricing strategy either reflected confidence or innumeracy — both are possible.

definition: The quality of having a ready insight; shrewdness
example: Her perspicacity in reading people made her valuable in every room she entered.

definition: The ability to make good judgments and quick decisions; keenness
example: Financial acumen without ethical acumen produces impressive numbers and interesting investigations.

definition: Brisk and cheerful readiness to do something
example: She responded with alacrity to challenges and glacially to administrative requests — sensible priorities.

definition: Self-confidence and composure, especially in difficult situations
example: She handled the ambush question with aplomb that suggested she'd prepared for exactly this.

definition: Mental calmness and composure, especially in difficult situations
example: His equanimity under fire was either hard-won wisdom or sociopathic detachment — possibly both.

definition: Composure or coolness, sometimes excessive, as shown in danger or under stress
example: Her sangfroid during the public failure was the only impressive thing about the whole episode.

definition: The ability to act or speak appropriately in social situations
example: His savoir-faire in the room was evident; his savoir-faire on email was another matter entirely.
